messages.subject: Problems to fit Mh2
parts:
Dear secr discussion list members,


I tried to fit Mh2 but did not succeed (this can happen but I got some errors message I could not understand so far see below). The remaining classical models and more complicated mixture models could be fitted. I tried different approaches using the default “Newton-Raphson”, the "Nelder-Mead" methods and by providing a list of starting values for D, g0 and sigma or starting models as well as using the conditional likelihood. When using the “Newton-Raphson”, the "Nelder-Mead" methods secr.fit finishes with warning code the same happens when setting the start to list of values. When setting start to Mbk (start=Mbk) secr.fit does not start and provides an error message (Error in parindx0 [[j]]: subscript out of bound). This happened also when setting the start to M0 or any other classic model I used so far. Although the model could not be fitted properly such warning message did not appear when setting the start to more complicated models such as secr.fit(capthist, mask=mask_prox, model = list(D~1, g0~h2, sigma~1), hcov='SEX'). Do I get an error message when setting start to the classic models because there are not enough parameters in these models (an/some init(s) are missing)? Des somebody have an explanation why this error message “Error in parindx0 [[j]]: subscript out of bound” appears?
Many thanks in advance


Best regards


Fridolin

messages.author: 0dbfcf0efe4ff8fe
messages.subject: Re: Problems to fit Mh2
parts:
Hi Fridolin,
That's right, models without h2 cannot be used as starting values when fitting models with h2, because some parameters (pmix) are absent.  Sparse data could explain why h2 models fail to fit when you don't provide any starting values. Be careful mixing the "hcov" formulation with other h2 models!  I don't know enough about the hcov formulation to be specific, but as I understand it when you use hcov = sex secr uses the mixture distribution to assign individuals of unknown sex to one of the two sexes, i.e. not to model addition heterogeneity among individuals.

Eric

Providing the starting values as a list is fine if it works.  What is the warning message when you fit the model?  Do you have enough occasions/recaptures to fit the h2 models?

messages.author: 0dbfcf0efe4ff8fe
messages.subject: Re: Problems to fit Mh2
parts:
Hi Fridolin,

It looks like you have enough recaptures to use the h2 models, I'm not sure why you're getting the probably maximization error message. Check the resulting model object for beta parameter estimates that are unrealistic, NaN, or have SE's = 0 or NA. When this happens, results are probably not reliable.

I would try fitting the models without providing any starting values, using all the optimization methods if the default gives the same message.

Also, are you setting both g0 and sigma ~ h2?  If so, I'd try models with the mixture applied to each parameter in isolation (maybe there's not enough information on movements to estimate sigma for 2 mixtures?).

Eric
